title: HAT — Higher Education Aptitude Test
description: A preparation course for the HEC Higher Education Aptitude Test (HAT), written for HAT-1 candidates in engineering, computing and the physical sciences. It covers the test structure and pacing, weighted study planning, the full quantitative and verbal syllabus, analytical reasoning, a timed-drill and mock programme, and an optional engineering background.
author: Underlayer

exercise_decls.question: What does the abbreviation HAT stand for?
exercise_decls.options: Higher Education Aptitude Test|Higher Academic Test|Higher Assessment of Teaching
exercise_decls.explanation: The HAT is the Higher Education Aptitude Test, used for admission to postgraduate programmes in Pakistan.
exercise_decls.hint1: The first word is the level of study it is used for.

exercise_decls.question: What is the primary purpose of the HAT?
exercise_decls.answer: To assess aptitude for postgraduate admission
exercise_decls.options: To replace the bachelor's degree|To assess aptitude for postgraduate admission|To test typing speed
exercise_decls.explanation: The test measures aptitude and readiness for postgraduate study, not previous degrees.
exercise_decls.hint1: It is an aptitude test, not a degree.

exercise_decls.question: A section carries 30% weightage. Out of 100 total marks, how many marks come from it?
exercise_decls.explanation: 30% of 100 marks is 30 marks. Weightage tells you where to spend study time.
exercise_decls.hint1: 30% means 30 per hundred.

exercise_decls.question: You have 40 questions and 40 minutes. What is your average time per question?
exercise_decls.options: 30 seconds|1 minute|3 minutes
exercise_decls.explanation: 40 questions in 40 minutes is one minute per question on average; hard questions must not exceed that budget.
exercise_decls.hint1: Divide the time by the number of questions.

exercise_decls.question: What is the best use of the final week before the test?
exercise_decls.answer: Timed full-length mocks and review of errors
exercise_decls.options: Learning brand new topics|Timed full-length mocks and review of errors|Resting entirely
exercise_decls.explanation: The final week is for timing, stamina and fixing known mistakes, not for starting new material.
exercise_decls.hint1: The clock is the skill that is hardest to build late.

exercise_decls.question: Why are past papers the highest-value practice?
exercise_decls.answer: They show the actual question types and timing
exercise_decls.options: They are easier than the real test|They show the actual question types and timing|They contain the real answers
exercise_decls.explanation: Past papers reveal the real question formats and pacing, which generic study material does not.
exercise_decls.hint1: Practice is valuable for its realism, not its difficulty.

exercise_decls.question: What is 15% of 240?
exercise_decls.explanation: 10% of 240 is 24 and 5% is 12, so 15% is 36.
exercise_decls.hint1: Build 15% from 10% plus 5%.

exercise_decls.question: What is 17 x 12?
exercise_decls.hint1: Split 12 into 10 plus 2.

exercise_decls.question: A price rises from 80 to 100. What is the percentage increase?
exercise_decls.explanation: The change is 20 on an original of 80, so 20/80 = 25%. Percentage change always divides by the original value.
exercise_decls.hint1: Divide the change by the original, not the new value.

exercise_decls.question: A value falls 20% and then rises 20%. Compared with its starting value it is:
exercise_decls.options: Back to the start|4% lower|4% higher
exercise_decls.explanation: 100 becomes 80, then 80 becomes 96, so it ends 4% below the start because the rise is computed on a smaller base.
exercise_decls.hint1: The two percentage changes are applied to different totals.

exercise_decls.question: Divide 180 in the ratio 2:3:4. What is the largest share?
exercise_decls.explanation: The parts total 9, so each part is 20; the largest share is 4 x 20 = 80.
exercise_decls.hint1: Add the ratio parts first to find one part.

exercise_decls.question: If 3 workers finish a job in 12 days, how long will 4 workers take at the same rate?
exercise_decls.options: 8 days|9 days|16 days
exercise_decls.explanation: The job takes 36 worker-days; 4 workers finish it in 36 / 4 = 9 days. This is inverse proportion.
exercise_decls.hint1: Find the total work in worker-days.

exercise_decls.question: Solve for x: 3x + 7 = 22
exercise_decls.explanation: Subtract 7 to get 3x = 15, then divide by 3 to get x = 5.
exercise_decls.hint1: Undo the addition before the multiplication.

exercise_decls.question: Factor x squared + 7x + 12.
exercise_decls.explanation: 3 and 4 multiply to 12 and add to 7, which is the coefficient of x.
exercise_decls.hint1: Find two numbers that multiply to 12 and add to 7.

exercise_decls.question: What is the area of a triangle with base 10 and height 6?
exercise_decls.explanation: Area is one half times base times height: 0.5 x 10 x 6 = 30.
exercise_decls.hint1: Do not forget the one-half factor.

exercise_decls.question: The three interior angles of a triangle always sum to:
exercise_decls.options: 90 degrees|180 degrees|360 degrees
exercise_decls.explanation: The interior angles of a Euclidean triangle sum to 180 degrees.
exercise_decls.hint1: It is the same total for every triangle.

exercise_decls.question: What is the mean of 4, 8, 10 and 14?
exercise_decls.explanation: The sum is 36 and there are four values, so the mean is 36 / 4 = 9.
exercise_decls.hint1: Add the values, then divide by how many there are.

exercise_decls.question: What is the probability of rolling an even number on a fair six-sided die?
exercise_decls.explanation: There are three even outcomes (2, 4, 6) out of six, so the probability is 3/6 = 1/2.
exercise_decls.hint1: Count the favourable outcomes out of six.

exercise_decls.question: 'Candid' most nearly means:
exercise_decls.options: deceitful|frank|hesitant
exercise_decls.explanation: Candid means open and honest, that is frank; a candid answer is a straightforward one.
exercise_decls.hint1: A candid photograph is unposed and honest.

exercise_decls.question: Which is the best way to learn vocabulary for the test?
exercise_decls.answer: Learn roots and words in context
exercise_decls.options: Memorise an alphabetical list|Learn roots and words in context|Read the whole dictionary nightly
exercise_decls.explanation: Roots let you decode unfamiliar words, and context fixes meaning; a bare list does not transfer to the exam.
exercise_decls.hint1: Look for the method that scales to words you have never seen.

exercise_decls.question: BOOK : READ :: PIANO : ?
exercise_decls.options: music|play|listen
exercise_decls.explanation: The relationship is object to the action performed on it: a book is read and a piano is played.
exercise_decls.hint1: State what you do with the first object.

exercise_decls.question: What is the first step in an analogy question?
exercise_decls.answer: State the relationship between the given pair
exercise_decls.options: Look for the longest option|State the relationship between the given pair|Choose the option you recognise
exercise_decls.explanation: Naming the relationship in a short phrase makes the matching option obvious and filters distractors.
exercise_decls.hint1: You cannot match a relationship you have not named.

exercise_decls.question: 'Although the plan was ambitious, it was ___.' Which word fits the signal?
exercise_decls.options: practical|impractical|approved
exercise_decls.explanation: Although signals contrast, so the second half must oppose the positive word ambitious.
exercise_decls.hint1: Although marks a contrast, not an addition.

exercise_decls.question: Which relationship does the signal word 'however' express?
exercise_decls.options: addition|contrast|cause and effect
exercise_decls.explanation: However marks a turn in direction, so the clause that follows opposes what came before.
exercise_decls.hint1: It behaves like 'but'.

exercise_decls.question: Find the error: 'The list of items are long.' Which word is wrong?
exercise_decls.options: list|are|long
exercise_decls.explanation: The subject is the singular 'list', so the verb must be 'is'. The plural 'items' sits between them as a decoy.
exercise_decls.hint1: Find the real subject, ignoring the phrase after 'of'.

exercise_decls.question: Complete correctly: 'He is senior ___ me.'
exercise_decls.options: than|to|of
exercise_decls.explanation: Senior, junior, superior and inferior take 'to' rather than 'than'.
exercise_decls.hint1: This word is not like 'taller than'.

exercise_decls.question: Which question type should usually be answered last?
exercise_decls.options: Specific detail|Main idea|Vocabulary in context
exercise_decls.explanation: Answering the specific questions first tells you what the passage says, which makes the main-idea question cheap.
exercise_decls.hint1: Order the questions so that the later ones benefit from the earlier ones.

exercise_decls.question: An inference answer choice is usually wrong when it:
exercise_decls.answer: Uses extreme words and goes beyond the passage
exercise_decls.options: Restates the text|Uses extreme words and goes beyond the passage|Is shorter than the others
exercise_decls.explanation: The correct inference must be true from the text alone; words like always, never and only push it past the evidence.
exercise_decls.hint1: Look for overreach, not length.

exercise_decls.question: How do you test whether an option is a required assumption?
exercise_decls.answer: Negate it and see if the argument collapses
exercise_decls.options: Ask whether it sounds plausible|Negate it and see if the argument collapses|Check whether you agree with it
exercise_decls.explanation: If the argument fails once the option is denied, the option was required for the conclusion to hold.
exercise_decls.hint1: The test is structural, not about agreement.

exercise_decls.question: Ice cream sales and drowning deaths rise together, and the author blames ice cream. The flaw is:
exercise_decls.options: False dilemma|Correlation treated as causation|Circular reasoning
exercise_decls.explanation: A third factor such as summer heat drives both, so the observed association does not establish cause.
exercise_decls.hint1: Two things moving together is not proof of cause.

exercise_decls.question: Given 'if P then Q', which statement must be true?
exercise_decls.answer: If not Q, then not P
exercise_decls.options: If Q, then P|If not Q, then not P|If not P, then not Q
exercise_decls.explanation: That is the contrapositive, which is equivalent to the original rule; the converse and inverse are not valid.
exercise_decls.hint1: Reverse the order and negate both parts.

exercise_decls.question: Four files P, Q, R, S are reviewed one per day. S is immediately after Q, Q is not first, and P is before R. What is true in every valid arrangement?
exercise_decls.options: P is reviewed last|P is reviewed first|R is reviewed second in every case
exercise_decls.explanation: The two valid orders are P, Q, S, R and P, R, Q, S, so P is first in both.
exercise_decls.hint1: Enumerate the arrangements before reading the options.

exercise_decls.question: Enrolment rises from a total of 300 to 350. What is the percentage increase?
exercise_decls.explanation: The change is 50 on an original of 300, so 50 / 300 = 16.7%. Dividing by 350 gives the wrong 14.3%.
exercise_decls.hint1: Divide by the original total.

exercise_decls.question: Department A goes from 120 to 150 and department B from 80 to 100. Which grew faster in percentage terms?
exercise_decls.answer: They grew at the same rate
exercise_decls.options: Department A|Department B|They grew at the same rate
exercise_decls.explanation: A grew 30/120 = 25% and B grew 20/80 = 25%, so the smaller absolute increase is the same percentage rate.
exercise_decls.hint1: Compute each change as a fraction of its own original.

exercise_decls.question: What comes next: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?
exercise_decls.explanation: The differences are 3, 5, 7 and 9, so the next is 11 and 26 + 11 = 37.
exercise_decls.hint1: Write the differences between consecutive terms.

exercise_decls.question: What comes next: 3, 6, 12, 24, ?
exercise_decls.explanation: The terms double each time, so the next is 48. This is a geometric series with ratio 2.
exercise_decls.hint1: Check the ratio rather than the difference.

exercise_decls.question: A force acts on a 4 kg mass producing an acceleration of 3 m/s squared. What is the force?
exercise_decls.explanation: From F = ma: 4 x 3 = 12 newtons.
exercise_decls.hint1: Newton's second law multiplies mass by acceleration.

exercise_decls.question: A car starts from rest and accelerates at 2 m/s squared for 5 s. What is its final velocity?
exercise_decls.explanation: Using v = u + at with u = 0: v = 2 x 5 = 10 m/s.
exercise_decls.hint1: Starting from rest means the initial velocity is zero.

exercise_decls.question: What is the binary number 1101 in decimal?
exercise_decls.explanation: The place values 8, 4, 2 and 1 give 8 + 4 + 1 = 13, since the twos place is zero.
exercise_decls.hint1: Add the place values where a 1 appears.

exercise_decls.question: How many distinct values can a single byte represent?
exercise_decls.explanation: A byte is 8 bits, so it holds 2 raised to the 8th power, which is 256 values from 0 to 255.
exercise_decls.hint1: A byte has 8 bits.

exercise_decls.question: When does an XOR gate output a 1?
exercise_decls.options: When both inputs are 1|When the two inputs differ|When both inputs are 0
exercise_decls.explanation: XOR is the exclusive OR: it outputs 1 for the rows 0 and 1, and 1 and 0, and 0 when the inputs are equal.
exercise_decls.hint1: It is true when exactly one input is true.

exercise_decls.question: Applying De Morgan's law, NOT(A AND B) equals:
exercise_decls.options: NOT A AND NOT B|(NOT A) OR (NOT B)|A AND B
exercise_decls.explanation: Negate each input and flip the gate: a negated AND becomes an OR of the negated inputs.
exercise_decls.hint1: Negate the inputs and swap AND for OR.

exercise_decls.question: The HAT has 100 questions and 120 minutes. About how long may you spend per question on average?
exercise_decls.options: 45 seconds|72 seconds|120 seconds
exercise_decls.explanation: 120 minutes is 7,200 seconds, and 7,200 divided by 100 is 72 seconds per question.
exercise_decls.hint1: Divide the total seconds by the number of questions.

exercise_decls.question: Which section of HAT-1 carries the most questions?
exercise_decls.options: Verbal Reasoning|Quantitative Reasoning|Analytical Reasoning
exercise_decls.explanation: HAT-1 weights quantitative reasoning at 40%, so it contributes about 40 of the 100 questions.
exercise_decls.hint1: It has the largest weightage.

exercise_decls.question: The HAT applies no negative marking. What is the best policy for a question you cannot solve?
exercise_decls.answer: Eliminate what you can and guess
exercise_decls.options: Leave it blank|Eliminate what you can and guess|Spend five minutes on it
exercise_decls.explanation: With no penalty for a wrong answer, a blank is a guaranteed zero while a guess retains a chance of a mark.
exercise_decls.hint1: A wrong answer costs nothing.

exercise_decls.question: What does triage mean on a timed test?
exercise_decls.answer: Deciding quickly which questions to do now, later or never
exercise_decls.options: Answering questions in strict order|Deciding quickly which questions to do now, later or never|Guessing every question at random
exercise_decls.explanation: Triage is the allocation of a fixed time budget to the questions most likely to pay off.
exercise_decls.hint1: It is about allocating time, not effort.

exercise_decls.question: Is 4,815 divisible by 9?
exercise_decls.answer: Yes, the digit sum 18 is a multiple of 9
exercise_decls.options: No, it is odd|Yes, the digit sum 18 is a multiple of 9|Only if it is also even
exercise_decls.explanation: The divisibility rule for 9 is that the digit sum must be a multiple of 9; 4+8+1+5 = 18.
exercise_decls.hint1: Add the digits and test the sum.

exercise_decls.question: What is the units digit of 7 to the power 43?
exercise_decls.explanation: Powers of 7 cycle 7, 9, 3, 1 with length 4; 43 leaves remainder 3, so the units digit is the third element, 3.
exercise_decls.hint1: Find the exponent's position in the four-term cycle.

exercise_decls.question: What is the HCF of 24 and 36?
exercise_decls.explanation: 24 = 2 cubed x 3 and 36 = 2 squared x 3 squared. The HCF takes each shared prime to its lowest power: 2 squared x 3 = 12.
exercise_decls.hint1: Factor both numbers, then take the shared primes to their lowest powers.

exercise_decls.question: What is the LCM of 8 and 12?
exercise_decls.explanation: 8 = 2 cubed and 12 = 2 squared x 3. The LCM takes every prime to its highest power: 2 cubed x 3 = 24. The product 96 double-counts the shared factors.
exercise_decls.hint1: Take every prime that appears in either number to its highest power.

exercise_decls.question: What is 5/8 written as a decimal?
exercise_decls.explanation: Five eighths is five times 0.125, which is 0.625.
exercise_decls.hint1: Use the eighths row of the conversion table.

exercise_decls.question: What is 3/8 expressed as a percentage?
exercise_decls.explanation: 3/8 is 0.375, and 0.375 times 100 is 37.5 percent.
exercise_decls.hint1: Convert to a decimal first, then multiply by 100.

exercise_decls.question: The mean of four numbers is 9. Three of them are 4, 10 and 12. What is the fourth?
exercise_decls.explanation: The total is 4 times 9 = 36; the three known numbers sum to 26, so the fourth is 10.
exercise_decls.hint1: Start from the total, not the average.

exercise_decls.question: A test scored 60 counts twice as much as a test scored 90. What is the weighted mean?
exercise_decls.hint1: Weight each score by how much it counts.

exercise_decls.question: A car travels 180 km in 2 hours 30 minutes. What is its average speed?
exercise_decls.options: 60 km/h|72 km/h|90 km/h
exercise_decls.explanation: 2 hours 30 minutes is 2.5 hours, and 180 divided by 2.5 is 72 km/h.
exercise_decls.hint1: Convert the time to decimal hours first.

exercise_decls.question: Two trains leave one station in opposite directions at 60 and 80 km/h. How far apart are they after 2 hours?
exercise_decls.explanation: In opposite directions the speeds add: 60 + 80 = 140 km/h, and 140 x 2 = 280 km.
exercise_decls.hint1: Opposite directions means combined speed.

exercise_decls.question: A finishes a job in 12 days and B in 6 days. Working together, how long do they take?
exercise_decls.options: 3 days|4 days|9 days
exercise_decls.explanation: Their combined rate is 1/12 + 1/6 = 3/12 = 1/4 of the job per day, so the job takes 4 days.
exercise_decls.hint1: Add the rates, do not average the times.

exercise_decls.question: Three identical pipes fill a tank in 6 hours. If one pipe is closed, how long do the other two take?
exercise_decls.options: 4 hours|9 hours|12 hours
exercise_decls.explanation: The tank needs 3 x 6 = 18 pipe-hours; two pipes deliver it in 18 / 2 = 9 hours.
exercise_decls.hint1: Convert to total work in pipe-hours.

exercise_decls.question: In how many distinct orders can 4 different books be arranged on a shelf?
exercise_decls.explanation: The number of arrangements is 4 factorial, which is 4 x 3 x 2 x 1 = 24.
exercise_decls.hint1: Each choice reduces the next by one.

exercise_decls.question: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of exactly one head?
exercise_decls.explanation: Of the four equally likely outcomes, two have exactly one head, so the probability is 2/4 = 1/2.
exercise_decls.hint1: List the four outcomes.

exercise_decls.question: In a timed quantitative drill, what should you do when a question runs past its time budget?
exercise_decls.answer: Mark it, guess if possible, and move on
exercise_decls.options: Keep working until it is solved|Mark it, guess if possible, and move on|Restart the section
exercise_decls.explanation: A drill trains the budget as much as the mathematics; protecting the budget is the point.
exercise_decls.hint1: The drill rehearses the real test's pacing.

exercise_decls.question: Why should drill questions be timed?
exercise_decls.answer: Timing builds the pacing the real test requires
exercise_decls.options: Timing makes the questions harder|Timing builds the pacing the real test requires|Timing reduces accuracy for no benefit
exercise_decls.explanation: The clock is part of the test; untimed practice cannot train it.
exercise_decls.hint1: The real test has a clock.

exercise_decls.question: Choose the best synonym for lucid.
exercise_decls.options: murky|clear|lengthy
exercise_decls.explanation: Lucid means clear and easy to understand, especially of writing or explanation.
exercise_decls.hint1: Think of something easy to follow.

exercise_decls.question: What is the antonym of frugal?
exercise_decls.options: thrifty|extravagant|cautious
exercise_decls.explanation: Frugal means economical or sparing; its opposite is extravagant, meaning wasteful in spending.
exercise_decls.hint1: Antonyms are opposites, not near-synonyms.

exercise_decls.question: A blank introduced by the word However must:
exercise_decls.answer: oppose or qualify what came before
exercise_decls.options: continue the same direction|oppose or qualify what came before|give an example of the same claim
exercise_decls.explanation: However marks a contrast, so the missing sentence must turn against the preceding direction.
exercise_decls.hint1: However behaves like but.

exercise_decls.question: Which completion is most likely wrong in a paragraph-completion item?
exercise_decls.answer: One that introduces a topic the passage never raised
exercise_decls.options: One that continues the passage's argument|One that introduces a topic the passage never raised|One that restates the passage's conclusion
exercise_decls.explanation: A completion must stay inside the passage's scope; a new topic is off-topic even if it is true.
exercise_decls.hint1: Check scope before style.

exercise_decls.question: Choose the correct verb: The list of items ___ long.
exercise_decls.options: are|is|were
exercise_decls.explanation: The subject is the singular noun list; the phrase of items is a modifier and does not change the number.
exercise_decls.hint1: Find the real subject, ignoring the of-phrase.

exercise_decls.question: Choose the correct verb: Neither of the boys ___ finished.
exercise_decls.options: have|has|having
exercise_decls.explanation: Neither is singular, so it takes the singular verb has.
exercise_decls.hint1: Neither and either are singular.

exercise_decls.question: Complete correctly: She is proficient ___ three languages.
exercise_decls.options: at|in|with
exercise_decls.explanation: The fixed collocation is proficient in a subject or skill.
exercise_decls.hint1: It is a fixed word partnership.

exercise_decls.question: Complete correctly: The report complies ___ the new rules.
exercise_decls.options: to|with|for
exercise_decls.explanation: Comply takes the preposition with: to comply with a rule.
exercise_decls.hint1: Learn the verb and its preposition together.

exercise_decls.question: Why is recognising the question type valuable under time?
exercise_decls.answer: It tells you which procedure to apply immediately
exercise_decls.options: It makes the passage shorter|It tells you which procedure to apply immediately|It guarantees a correct answer
exercise_decls.explanation: Each verbal type has a routine; naming the type triggers the routine without deliberation.
exercise_decls.hint1: Each type has its own method.

exercise_decls.question: In a verbal drill, what should you do with a question you cannot decide within its budget?
exercise_decls.answer: Choose the best option and continue
exercise_decls.options: Leave it blank|Choose the best option and continue|Re-read the passage three times
exercise_decls.explanation: With no negative marking, an answered best guess beats a blank and protects the remaining time.
exercise_decls.hint1: A blank cannot score.

exercise_decls.question: Two quantities rise and fall together. What can always be concluded?
exercise_decls.options: One causes the other|Only that they are correlated|The second causes the first
exercise_decls.explanation: Association alone establishes correlation, not the direction or existence of causation.
exercise_decls.hint1: Moving together is not proof of cause.

exercise_decls.question: Ice-cream sales and drowning deaths rise together in summer. What best explains the link?
exercise_decls.options: Ice cream causes drowning|A common cause: warm weather|Drowning causes ice-cream sales
exercise_decls.explanation: Warm weather drives both swimming and ice-cream purchases, so a third factor explains the correlation.
exercise_decls.hint1: Look for a factor that drives both.

exercise_decls.question: In a row of 5 people, if A sits immediately to the left of B, in how many positions can the block (A,B) sit?
exercise_decls.explanation: A block of two consecutive seats can start at positions 1 through 4 in a row of five.
exercise_decls.hint1: Slide the block along the row.

exercise_decls.question: How many distinct circular arrangements are there of n distinct people?
exercise_decls.options: n factorial|(n-1) factorial|n factorial divided by 2
exercise_decls.explanation: Fix one person to remove the rotational symmetry, leaving (n-1)! arrangements of the rest.
exercise_decls.hint1: Fixing one seat removes rotation.

exercise_decls.question: In an ordering puzzle, what is the first thing to record?
exercise_decls.answer: The fixed constraints as rules or a diagram
exercise_decls.options: The answer options first|The fixed constraints as rules or a diagram|The final question
exercise_decls.explanation: Constraints are the raw material; a compact diagram or list of rules makes them usable.
exercise_decls.hint1: Start from what is fixed.

exercise_decls.question: A must-be-true question asks for a statement that is true:
exercise_decls.options: in at least one arrangement|in every valid arrangement|in the arrangement you drew first
exercise_decls.explanation: Must be true means true across all arrangements that satisfy the constraints, not just one.
exercise_decls.hint1: Distinguish must from could.

exercise_decls.question: All poets are dreamers. Some dreamers are teachers. Which must be true?
exercise_decls.options: Some poets are teachers|Nothing further follows about teachers|All teachers are poets
exercise_decls.explanation: The teachers may be dreamers who are not poets, so no link between poets and teachers is guaranteed.
exercise_decls.hint1: Draw the two circles and check the overlap.

exercise_decls.question: All engineers are graduates. No graduate is unemployed. Which must be true?
exercise_decls.options: Some engineers are unemployed|No engineer is unemployed|All graduates are engineers
exercise_decls.explanation: Engineers are graduates, and no graduate is unemployed, so no engineer can be unemployed.
exercise_decls.hint1: Chain the two statements.

exercise_decls.question: A man walks 3 km north, then 4 km east. How far is he from the start?
exercise_decls.options: 5 km|7 km|1 km
exercise_decls.explanation: The two legs are perpendicular, so the distance is the hypotenuse of a 3-4-5 right triangle.
exercise_decls.hint1: Use the right-triangle rule.

exercise_decls.question: If X is the brother of Y's father, how is X related to Y?
exercise_decls.options: uncle|brother|cousin
exercise_decls.explanation: The brother of one's father is one's uncle.
exercise_decls.hint1: Draw the family tree.

exercise_decls.question: If CAT is written as DBU, each letter shifted one forward, how is DOG written?
exercise_decls.options: EPH|DPH|FQI
exercise_decls.explanation: Shift each letter of DOG one forward: D to E, O to P, G to H.
exercise_decls.hint1: Apply the same shift to each letter.

exercise_decls.question: In a code each letter is replaced by the letter two before it. What does G decode to?
exercise_decls.options: E|I|H
exercise_decls.explanation: Two letters before G in the alphabet is E.
exercise_decls.hint1: Count backwards two places.

exercise_decls.question: In a data-sufficiency item, what decides whether the information is enough?
exercise_decls.answer: Whether the question can be answered without extra assumptions
exercise_decls.options: How large the numbers look|Whether the question can be answered without extra assumptions|Which statement is longer
exercise_decls.explanation: Sufficiency asks whether the given facts uniquely determine the answer, not for the answer itself.
exercise_decls.hint1: The question is about sufficiency, not computation.

exercise_decls.question: What should you avoid doing in a data-sufficiency question?
exercise_decls.answer: Computing the exact answer when only sufficiency is asked
exercise_decls.options: Testing each statement separately|Computing the exact answer when only sufficiency is asked|Using the question's constraints
exercise_decls.explanation: Full computation wastes time; you only need to know whether the data pins the answer down.
exercise_decls.hint1: Decide, do not solve.

exercise_decls.question: What is the main purpose of a timed analytical drill?
exercise_decls.answer: To make the standard procedures automatic and fast
exercise_decls.options: To learn new puzzle types|To make the standard procedures automatic and fast|To memorise answers
exercise_decls.explanation: The analytical section punishes hesitation; the drill converts known methods into reflex.
exercise_decls.hint1: The drill trains speed on known methods.

exercise_decls.question: How does could-be-true differ from must-be-true?
exercise_decls.answer: It only needs to hold in some valid arrangement
exercise_decls.options: It must hold in every arrangement|It only needs to hold in some valid arrangement|It is always false
exercise_decls.explanation: Could be true asks for existence in at least one valid arrangement; must be true requires all.
exercise_decls.hint1: One is existential, the other universal.

exercise_decls.question: Why is a full-length mock under real timing valuable?
exercise_decls.answer: It trains pacing and stamina as well as knowledge
exercise_decls.options: It teaches new content|It trains pacing and stamina as well as knowledge|It guarantees a higher score
exercise_decls.explanation: A mock rehearses the clock, fatigue and section order, which untimed practice never does.
exercise_decls.hint1: The clock is part of the test.

exercise_decls.question: What should you do immediately after a mock?
exercise_decls.answer: Review every error by rule and record it in the error log
exercise_decls.options: Immediately take another mock|Review every error by rule and record it in the error log|Discard the paper
exercise_decls.explanation: The mock's value is in the diagnosis; unreviewed errors repeat.
exercise_decls.hint1: The point is the feedback, not the score.

exercise_decls.question: What is the purpose of an error log?
exercise_decls.answer: To turn repeated mistakes into specific rules to fix
exercise_decls.options: To record your scores|To turn repeated mistakes into specific rules to fix|To count how many questions you did
exercise_decls.explanation: Listing the rule behind each mistake makes the weak spots visible and fixable.
exercise_decls.hint1: Record the rule, not the score.

exercise_decls.question: A good error-log entry records:
exercise_decls.answer: the question type, the rule missed, and the fix
exercise_decls.options: only the wrong answer|the question type, the rule missed, and the fix|only the time you took
exercise_decls.explanation: Type, rule and fix turn a single error into a reusable lesson.
exercise_decls.hint1: It should be actionable next session.

exercise_decls.question: Why is do-my-best a weak score target?
exercise_decls.answer: It cannot be measured, so it cannot guide practice
exercise_decls.options: It is too high|It cannot be measured, so it cannot guide practice|It is too low
exercise_decls.explanation: A target must be checkable against results; an unmeasurable target cannot direct weekly work.
exercise_decls.hint1: Targets must be measurable.

exercise_decls.question: HAT-1 weights the sections 40/30/30. With 70% quantitative and 60% in each other section, what is the overall percentage?
exercise_decls.hint1: Apply the weights to each section.

exercise_decls.question: How many questions does the HAT contain, and how long is the test?
exercise_decls.options: 80 questions in 100 minutes|100 questions in 120 minutes|120 questions in 100 minutes
exercise_decls.explanation: The HAT is 100 multiple-choice questions in 120 minutes.
exercise_decls.hint1: About one minute and twelve seconds each.

exercise_decls.question: With no negative marking and one minute left, what should you do with unanswered questions?
exercise_decls.answer: Answer all of them, guessing if needed
exercise_decls.options: Leave them blank|Answer all of them, guessing if needed|Answer only the first one
exercise_decls.explanation: A blank is certainly zero; a guessed answer keeps a chance of a mark at no cost.
exercise_decls.hint1: Every question deserves an answer.

exercise_decls.question: Why sit a cold diagnostic before you begin studying?
exercise_decls.answer: To find which sections need the most work
exercise_decls.options: To score highly on the first attempt|To find which sections need the most work|To replace the rest of studying
exercise_decls.explanation: A cold diagnostic is a measurement, not a performance; its value is telling you where to spend the next weeks.
exercise_decls.hint1: It is evidence for planning.

exercise_decls.question: A candidate scores quantitative 22/40, verbal 18/30 and analytical 14/30. Which section should get the most work?
exercise_decls.options: Quantitative|Verbal|Analytical
exercise_decls.explanation: Analytical is furthest from its potential at 47%, so it has the most headroom.
exercise_decls.hint1: Compare each section's percentage.

exercise_decls.question: Simplify 2 to the power 5 times 2 to the power 3.
exercise_decls.options: 2 to the power 8|2 to the power 15|4 to the power 8
exercise_decls.explanation: Multiplying powers of the same base adds the indices: 5 + 3 = 8.
exercise_decls.hint1: Add the exponents when the bases match.

exercise_decls.question: Simplify the square root of 50 plus the square root of 18.
exercise_decls.options: 8 times the square root of 2|the square root of 68|68
exercise_decls.explanation: Root 50 is 5 root 2 and root 18 is 3 root 2, giving 8 root 2.
exercise_decls.hint1: Simplify each surd to a multiple of root 2 first.

exercise_decls.question: What are the roots of x squared minus 5x plus 6 equals 0?
exercise_decls.options: 2 and 3|minus 2 and minus 3|1 and 6
exercise_decls.explanation: 2 and 3 multiply to 6 and add to 5, matching the coefficients.
exercise_decls.hint1: Find two numbers that multiply to 6 and add to 5.

exercise_decls.question: For a quadratic ax squared plus bx plus c equals 0, the sum of the roots is:
exercise_decls.options: b over a|minus b over a|c over a
exercise_decls.explanation: The sum of the roots is minus b over a; their product is c over a.
exercise_decls.hint1: It is the negative of the x coefficient over the leading coefficient.

exercise_decls.question: What is the 10th term of the arithmetic sequence 3, 7, 11, ...?
exercise_decls.explanation: The nth term is a plus (n minus 1)d: 3 plus 9 times 4 equals 39.
exercise_decls.hint1: Find the common difference first.

exercise_decls.question: What comes next: 2, 6, 18, 54, ...?
exercise_decls.explanation: Each term is three times the previous one, so 54 times 3 is 162.
exercise_decls.hint1: Check the ratio, not the difference.

exercise_decls.question: What is the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm, using pi equals 22 over 7?
exercise_decls.options: 1540 cubic cm|440 cubic cm|220 cubic cm
exercise_decls.explanation: Volume is pi r squared h: 22/7 times 49 times 10 equals 1540.
exercise_decls.hint1: Area of the base times the height.

exercise_decls.question: What is the area of a circle of radius 7 cm, using pi equals 22 over 7?
exercise_decls.options: 154 square cm|44 square cm|49 square cm
exercise_decls.explanation: Area is pi r squared: 22/7 times 49 equals 154.
exercise_decls.hint1: Do not confuse area with circumference.

exercise_decls.question: What is the distance between the points (2,1) and (6,9)?
exercise_decls.options: the square root of 80|the square root of 68|10
exercise_decls.explanation: The differences are 4 and 8, and 16 plus 64 equals 80.
exercise_decls.hint1: Use the distance formula on the two coordinate differences.

exercise_decls.question: What is the slope of the line through (2,1) and (6,9)?
exercise_decls.options: 2|one half|minus 2
exercise_decls.explanation: Slope is the change in y over the change in x: 8 divided by 4 equals 2.
exercise_decls.hint1: Rise over run.

exercise_decls.question: A number increased by 30 percent of itself equals 91. What is the number?
exercise_decls.explanation: The number times 1.3 equals 91, so the number is 91 divided by 1.3, which is 70.
exercise_decls.hint1: Write the sentence as an equation before solving.

exercise_decls.question: In word problems, the word of usually signals:
exercise_decls.options: addition|multiplication|division
exercise_decls.explanation: Of means multiply: a fraction of a quantity is that fraction times the quantity.
exercise_decls.hint1: Think of one half of 10.

exercise_decls.question: An item costs Rs 800 and sells for Rs 1000. What is the profit percent?
exercise_decls.options: 20 percent|25 percent|80 percent
exercise_decls.explanation: Profit is 200 on a cost of 800, so 200/800 equals 25 percent.
exercise_decls.hint1: Profit percent is on the cost price.

exercise_decls.question: Profit percent is always calculated on:
exercise_decls.options: the selling price|the cost price|the marked price
exercise_decls.explanation: Profit and loss percentages use the cost price as the base; discounts use the marked price.
exercise_decls.hint1: Identify the base before dividing.

exercise_decls.question: What is the simple interest on Rs 10,000 at 10 percent per year for 2 years?
exercise_decls.explanation: Simple interest is PRT/100: 10,000 times 10 times 2 divided by 100 equals 2,000.
exercise_decls.hint1: No compounding in simple interest.

exercise_decls.question: What is the compound interest on Rs 10,000 at 10 percent per year for 2 years?
exercise_decls.explanation: The amount is 10,000 times 1.1 squared, which is 12,100, so interest is 2,100.
exercise_decls.hint1: The second year earns interest on the first year's interest.

exercise_decls.question: Choose the correct completion: The committee reviewed the plan, approved the budget, and ___ the schedule.
exercise_decls.options: adjusted|adjusting|to adjust
exercise_decls.explanation: The list must be parallel, so all three verbs share the same past-tense form.
exercise_decls.hint1: Keep items in a list in the same grammatical form.

exercise_decls.question: In sentence correction, the option meaning no change is:
exercise_decls.options: never correct|sometimes correct|always correct
exercise_decls.explanation: A sentence may already be correct, so no change is a genuine possibility, though often a trap.
exercise_decls.hint1: Do not assume the sentence is faulty.

exercise_decls.question: An inference in a reading passage must be:
exercise_decls.options: true in real life|supported by the passage|the author's exact words
exercise_decls.explanation: An inference is unstated but must be justified by the text, not by outside knowledge.
exercise_decls.hint1: Distinguish stated from implied.

exercise_decls.question: The author's attitude is best judged from:
exercise_decls.answer: the tone words in the passage
exercise_decls.options: your own opinion|the tone words in the passage|the title alone
exercise_decls.explanation: Tone is carried by the author's word choices, not by the reader's reaction.
exercise_decls.hint1: Look at how the author describes things.

exercise_decls.question: Choose the correct form: She ___ here since 2019.
exercise_decls.options: works|has worked|worked
exercise_decls.explanation: Since a point in the past with a present result takes the present perfect.
exercise_decls.hint1: Since pairs with the perfect tense.

exercise_decls.question: Choose the correct form: If I ___ rich, I would travel.
exercise_decls.options: am|were|will be
exercise_decls.explanation: The second conditional uses were for all persons: If I were rich, I would travel.
exercise_decls.hint1: It is a hypothetical, not a fact.

exercise_decls.question: Which punctuation correctly joins two independent clauses?
exercise_decls.options: a comma|a semicolon|nothing
exercise_decls.explanation: A semicolon joins two independent clauses; a comma alone creates a comma splice.
exercise_decls.hint1: A comma is not strong enough on its own.

exercise_decls.question: Choose the correct possessive: The dog wagged ___ tail.
exercise_decls.options: it's|its|its'
exercise_decls.explanation: Its is the possessive; it's is only the contraction of it is.
exercise_decls.hint1: Test whether it is short for it is.

exercise_decls.question: An assumption in a statement is:
exercise_decls.answer: an unstated premise the statement depends on
exercise_decls.options: a stated fact|an unstated premise the statement depends on|the conclusion
exercise_decls.explanation: An assumption is not written down but is required for the statement to make sense.
exercise_decls.hint1: It is hidden, not stated.

exercise_decls.question: The negation test for an assumption asks:
exercise_decls.answer: whether the statement fails if the assumption is false
exercise_decls.options: whether the assumption is popular|whether the statement fails if the assumption is false|whether the assumption is stated
exercise_decls.explanation: If denying the assumption destroys the statement, the assumption was required.
exercise_decls.hint1: Deny it and see what happens.

exercise_decls.question: A conclusion follows from the statements only if it is:
exercise_decls.options: plausible in real life|necessarily implied by the statements|mentioned in the statements
exercise_decls.explanation: The conclusion must be forced by the statements, not merely believable or restated.
exercise_decls.hint1: Follows means must follow.

exercise_decls.question: How does must follow differ from might follow?
exercise_decls.answer: Must follow is guaranteed by the statements
exercise_decls.options: Must follow is merely more likely|Must follow is guaranteed by the statements|They are the same thing
exercise_decls.explanation: Must follow holds in every case the statements allow; might follow only needs one case.
exercise_decls.hint1: Must is universal, might is existential.

exercise_decls.question: A strong argument is one that is:
exercise_decls.answer: relevant and directly supports or attacks the proposal
exercise_decls.options: emotional and forceful|relevant and directly supports or attacks the proposal|long and detailed
exercise_decls.explanation: Strength comes from relevance and direct bearing on the proposal, not from force or length.
exercise_decls.hint1: Judge the link to the proposal.

exercise_decls.question: Which argument is weak?
exercise_decls.answer: Everyone knows the plan is bad.
exercise_decls.options: The plan costs more than the budget allows.|Everyone knows the plan is bad.|The plan would double capacity at the same cost.
exercise_decls.explanation: An appeal to what everyone knows is vague and unsupported, so it is weak.
exercise_decls.hint1: Look for relevance and evidence.

exercise_decls.question: A good course of action is:
exercise_decls.options: extreme and decisive|feasible, relevant and proportionate|vague and general
exercise_decls.explanation: An action must be practical, address the problem, and not overreach.
exercise_decls.hint1: Reject extremes and vague sentiments.

exercise_decls.question: Which is the weakest course of action for rising accidents at a junction?
exercise_decls.answer: The authorities should do something about it.
exercise_decls.options: Install a speed camera at the junction.|The authorities should do something about it.|Retrain the traffic staff within three months.
exercise_decls.explanation: The vague option names no concrete, checkable action.
exercise_decls.hint1: A course of action must be specific.

exercise_decls.question: If A is selected then B must be selected. Which statement is equivalent?
exercise_decls.answer: If B is not selected, then A is not selected
exercise_decls.options: If B is selected, then A must be selected|If B is not selected, then A is not selected|A and B can never both be selected
exercise_decls.explanation: That is the contrapositive, which is logically equivalent to the original rule.
exercise_decls.hint1: Reverse and negate both parts.

exercise_decls.question: At least one of X and Y must be in the group means:
exercise_decls.answer: X or Y or both are in the group
exercise_decls.options: exactly one of X and Y is in|X or Y or both are in the group|neither X nor Y is in
exercise_decls.explanation: At least one allows either one or both, unlike exactly one.
exercise_decls.hint1: At least one includes both.

exercise_decls.question: On a one-way circuit A to B to C to D to E to A, a message from B to D uses exactly one intermediary. Which node is it?
exercise_decls.options: C|E|F
exercise_decls.explanation: The circuit gives B to C to D in two hops, so C is the single middle node. The radio lines do not connect B to D.
exercise_decls.hint1: Walk the arrows, counting only the middle node.

exercise_decls.question: Two-way radios link B to F, F to G and D to G. What is the minimum number of intermediaries for a message from F to A?
exercise_decls.explanation: F-G-D-E-A passes through G, D and E: three intermediaries. The route via B (F-B-C-D-E-A) needs four.
exercise_decls.hint1: Try the exit through G first; A itself has no radio.

exercise_decls.question: For two sets, n of A union B equals:
exercise_decls.answer: n(A) plus n(B) minus n(A intersection B)
exercise_decls.options: n(A) plus n(B)|n(A) plus n(B) minus n(A intersection B)|n(A) times n(B)
exercise_decls.explanation: The elements in both sets are counted twice, so the intersection is subtracted once.
exercise_decls.hint1: Correct for double counting.

exercise_decls.question: In a class, 20 like tea, 15 like coffee and 8 like both. How many like at least one?
exercise_decls.explanation: 20 plus 15 minus 8 equals 27 like at least one.
exercise_decls.hint1: Use inclusion-exclusion.

exercise_decls.question: Which practice best supports long-term retention?
exercise_decls.options: Re-reading the notes|Testing yourself on the material|Highlighting the page
exercise_decls.explanation: Retrieval practice strengthens memory far more than passive review.
exercise_decls.hint1: Recall beats recognition.

exercise_decls.question: Spaced repetition means reviewing material:
exercise_decls.answer: just before you would forget it
exercise_decls.options: every day without exception|just before you would forget it|only in the week before the test
exercise_decls.explanation: Reviewing at increasing intervals, timed to when recall is about to fade, is the most efficient schedule.
exercise_decls.hint1: Space the reviews out.

exercise_decls.question: How should sleep be treated during preparation?
exercise_decls.answer: As part of preparation, not lost study time
exercise_decls.options: As wasted study time|As part of preparation, not lost study time|As important only for children
exercise_decls.explanation: Sleep consolidates memory and sustains accuracy, so it is a performance input, not a cost.
exercise_decls.hint1: Sleep is when learning is consolidated.

exercise_decls.question: The overactivity-underactivity cycle is:
exercise_decls.answer: studying intensely and then collapsing for days
exercise_decls.options: studying steadily every day|studying intensely and then collapsing for days|studying only at weekends
exercise_decls.explanation: Bursts followed by burnout produce less total learning than a steady, sustainable schedule.
exercise_decls.hint1: Consistency beats bursts.

exercise_decls.question: Which of these are valid IPv4 private address ranges? (select all)
exercise_decls.explanation: Private ranges are 10/8, 172.16/12, and 192.168/16. 8.8.8.0/24 is public (Google DNS).
exercise_decls.hint1: RFC 1918 defines exactly three private blocks.

exercise_decls.question: A 20% rise followed by a 20% fall leaves a net change of ___ percent (sign included, e.g. -4).
exercise_decls.explanation: 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96, which is a 4% fall.
exercise_decls.hint1: Multiply the multipliers, not the percentages.

exercise_decls.question: Match each shape to its area formula base×height applicability.
exercise_decls.options: Triangle|Parallelogram
exercise_decls.explanation: Both triangle and parallelogram areas are written in terms of a base and a corresponding height.
exercise_decls.hint1: Both use a base and a perpendicular height.

exercise_decls.question: Label the three HAT sections in order: Verbal, Analytical, Quantitative abilities.
exercise_decls.explanation: HAT-I sections are Verbal Ability, Analytical Ability, and Quantitative Ability.
exercise_decls.hint1: The paper is HAT-I with three numbered sections.

exercise_decls.question: If you spend 2 minutes per question on a 100-question paper with 120 minutes, what happens?
exercise_decls.options: You finish with time to spare|You run out of time|You finish exactly on time|You cannot answer all
exercise_decls.explanation: 2 minutes × 100 questions = 200 minutes, which exceeds the 120-minute limit.
exercise_decls.hint1: Multiply the per-question time by the number of questions.

certificate.title: HAT Preparation Complete
certificate.criteria: Complete all 69 concepts with 80% quiz accuracy

modules.title: Know the Arena
modules.description: What HAT-1 is, how it is weighted and paced, how to diagnose your baseline, and how to plan and execute eight weeks of preparation.

modules.title: Quantitative Reasoning
modules.description: Arithmetic and number sense, percentages, ratio and rate, algebra, sequences, geometry and mensuration, coordinate geometry, statistics, counting and probability, word problems, finance arithmetic, with a timed drill.

modules.title: Verbal Reasoning
modules.description: Vocabulary, synonyms and antonyms, analogies, sentence and paragraph completion, sentence correction, grammar and punctuation, idioms, reading comprehension, critical reading, and a timed drill.

modules.title: Analytical Reasoning
modules.description: Critical reasoning, statement-based question types, deduction and puzzles, syllogisms and set logic, relations and directions, coding, data sufficiency and interpretation, series, and a timed drill.

modules.title: The Athlete's Program
modules.description: Turning knowledge into a score: mock-test protocol, the error log, how to review, score targets, energy management and exam-day execution.

modules.title: Engineering Foundations (Optional)
modules.description: Optional background in mechanics, computing and digital logic for engineering and computing candidates. This is not a separate section of the HAT-1 paper.
